newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: ICE MARATHON TESTED DUTCH VIEWERS' ENDURANCE TOO.
newsitem.headline: ICE MARATHON TESTED DUTCH VIEWERS' ENDURANCE TOO.

text.p: Over 70 percent of the Netherlands' skating-mad population tuned in to the Elfstedentocht (Eleven cities tour) skate marathon held last Saturday, according to the Dutch TV ratings unit.

Some 11 million Dutch watched at least part of the traditional race, last able to be held in 1986, with a staggering 20 percent of the population in front of their sets for 15 hours or more, De Telegraaf newspaper said on Friday.

Sprout farmer Henk Angerent became an instant national hero winning the 200 km (125 mile) marathon, which started before dawn, in just under seven hours, but transmission continued until the last amateurs straggled home around midnight.

The race is held only in winters cold enough to produce six-inch-thick ice along the waterways linking 11 mediaeval Friesian towns. It attracted over 16,000 competitors and sparked a carnival mood across the whole nation.
